# Deliverables per workflow

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/gen-deliverables-doc.mjs from src/config/workflows.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every workflow def declares what it owes, per phase, in `src/config/workflows.json` (`deliverables[]`). Three consumers read that one list: this page, the board's artifacts modal (present / missing per deliverable) and the workflow-output Lambda, which refuses a registered markdown deliverable that does not follow its family template ([`blueprints/writing-standard.md`](../../blueprints/writing-standard.md)). Keys are relative to `workflows/<id>/shared/`; `*` is a single-segment glob.

## Five families, five templates

A deliverable belongs to one family, chosen by who reads it and what they do next. Each family has one template blueprint (reader questions as the `##` sections, in order, plus one real rewritten example) that every author loads before writing.

| Family | Written for | Sections (in order) | Template |
|---|---|---|---|
| `brief` | a human or agent who must approve or reject | `## Decision` `## Why it is ready` `## What needs your eye` `## After approval` | [template-brief](../../blueprints/template-brief.md) |
| `assessment` | whoever acts on the findings | `## Verdict` `## Findings` `## Not covered` `## Next actions` | [template-assessment](../../blueprints/template-assessment.md) |
| `spec` | whoever builds from it | `## Outcome` `## Scope` `## Approach` `## Acceptance` | [template-spec](../../blueprints/template-spec.md) |
| `record` | whoever tracks progress or audits later | `## Status` `## Timeline` `## Open items` | [template-record](../../blueprints/template-record.md) |
| `external` | the end audience (customer, counterparty, public) | `## Brief` `## Content` `## Notes for review` | [template-external](../../blueprints/template-external.md) |

Rules the lint enforces on every templated markdown deliverable: `# Title` first; the family's `##` sections present, in order, answer first; the lead section is prose of at most 80 words; extra `##` sections only after the template's; no ALL-CAPS heading or label, no `•` bullets. A refusal is returned to the agent with the missing sections and the template to load; nothing is written.

## Approvals: one standard, the question changes

Every human gate reads one decision document plus a `review-package-<gate>.json` ping derived from it (`summary` = the document's lead sentence, `bullets` = its attention items, `links` = the document first). The document is a `brief` wherever a human approves work; Spec and Plan Approval read the `spec` itself (its `## Outcome` is the decision line); Counsel Sign-off reads the `external` redlines with the contract review behind them.

| Gate | Defs | The reader decides | Reads |
|---|---|---|---|
| Spec Approval | software-delivery | Is this the right thing to build? | `requirements.md` (spec) |
| Plan Approval | software-delivery | Is this the right way to build it? | `design-doc-*.md` (spec) |
| Merge Approval | software-delivery, bug-fix, operator, dead-code-sweep | Does this merge? | `merge-brief.md` (brief) |
| Operator checkpoint | operator | Do we keep spending on this run? | `operator-status.md` (record) |
| Counsel Sign-off | legal | Do these redlines go to the counterparty? | `redlines.md` (external) |
| Deploy approval (pipeline ManualApproval, Telegram) | any CD-registered repo | Does this go live? | `cd-evidence/deploy-<sha>.md` (record) + the merge brief |

## Not on this list, on purpose

- The QA and CI **verdicts** are completion records (`completions/<ticket>.json`, `evidence_kind`, `ci_status`), not files; the evidence folders above are their attachments.
- `plan.md` (operator, playbook) and playbook `spec.md` keep their own exact sections because other blueprints read those headings; they are listed with template "own contract" and are not linted.
- Agent-folder copies (`workflows/<id>/<agentId>/...`) are staging; only `shared/` counts.

## Changing the list

Edit `deliverables[]` on the def in `src/config/workflows.json`, run `node scripts/gen-deliverables-doc.mjs`, and let `scripts/check-deliverables-parity.sh` tell you which blueprint still has to load the template. A new family needs a `blueprints/template-<family>.md` whose numbered section list matches `deliverableFamilies.<family>.sections` exactly (`src/lib/workflow/deliverables.test.ts` pins it).
